_: Need for Speed's track geometry is already metres — the disc stores 16.16
fixed point and nfs.Float divides by 65536, road segments 6 m apart — so
metresPerUnit is 1 and there is nothing to derive.
The spawn is the exported grid camera (webexport/main.go startCamera, itself
calibrated against the running game's camObj to 4 mm) with the driver's eye
height taken back off: segment 16, 96 m in, 2.9 m right of the centreline,
The two cars sit where a race starts, a lane either side of you.
_props: A 512 TR and a Diablo, one lane either side of where you stand.
The road is 8 lanes of 5 m spanning -20..+20, so lane centres are at
5*lane - 17.5: the grid camera's -2.902 sits in the lane at -2.5, and the
cars take the ones at -7.5 and +2.5.
rotY 0 = the model's own -Z, which is the direction the course runs and the
way the grid camera looks. Both models are 4.4-4.6 long on Z and sit on
y = 0, so they need no height offset. CHECK IN THE HEADSET: if they face
you rather than the horizon, both rotY become 180.
